title: @autoclosure: Lazy Logging
hints: `@autoclosure` wraps an argument in a closure, so it's only evaluated if you call it.
Guard on the level first; call `message()` only when it passes.
jsBridge: `@autoclosure` wraps an argument expression in a closure automatically, so `debugLog(expensive())` doesn't evaluate `expensive()` unless needed. In JS you'd pass `() => expensive()` by hand. `assert`, `??` and `&&` all rely on it.

compass.q: JS loggers take `() => msg` to be lazy. How does `@autoclosure` hide that at the call site, and is hiding it good?
Is an `@autoclosure` argument evaluated once or every time the closure is called?
`@autoclosure` vs `os.Logger`'s interpolation (which is lazy too): how does Apple's logger avoid formatting cost?
Why is `@autoclosure` discouraged for public APIs where evaluation isn't obvious?
